title.en: Dark studio product light from three soft boxes

summary: Shape a product against a dark ground with three rectangular soft boxes whose reflections describe the form.
objective: Each soft box is identifiable as a distinct reflection on a glossy sample, and the product edge separates from the background everywhere.
intent_signals: studio lighting on a dark background
the product edges disappear into the background
example_prompts: Light a device on a dark set so its silhouette stays crisp.
Show a metal part where the highlights describe its curvature.
Set a hero turntable for a small object without a white background.
not_for: Outdoor or environmental scenes that need a sky and a sun.
Any claim about the real output of studio fixtures, which needs measured photometric data.

principles: On a glossy product the lights are not seen directly, only their reflections. Sizing and placing those reflections is the whole job, and the source shape matters more than its intensity.
Edge separation comes before beauty. Every silhouette edge needs either a rim reflection or a background value different from the product at that point.
A dark set is not a black set. A vertical gradient behind the product gives the edge something to change against as it travels around the form.
Three sources is the working minimum for a hard-surface product: a large key to describe the main form, a broad low fill to open the shadow side, and a narrow strip behind for the edge.
The environment map is part of the lighting. At low intensity it fills the micro-reflections that discrete area lights leave empty.
implementation: Use RectAreaLights sized in metres: key 1.2 x 1.8 m, fill 2.0 x 1.2 m, rim strip 0.4 x 1.6 m, each aimed at the product with lookAt.
Initialise RectAreaLightUniformsLib before creating any RectAreaLight, or the lights contribute nothing.
Note that RectAreaLight casts no shadow in this renderer: get the contact shadow from a low-intensity DirectionalLight aimed down, or from a baked shadow-catcher plane under the product.
Add RoomEnvironment at 0.15 so smooth surfaces pick up broad reflections between the three panels; without it, metals go patchy.
Keep the background a vertical gradient from #0d0f12 to #1c2026 and check every silhouette edge against it as the product turns.
Keep bloom threshold high at 1.3: the soft box reflections are meant to stay legible as shapes, not to smear into glow.
observable_checks: A glossy test sphere shows three distinct rectangular reflections whose proportions match the stated panel sizes.
Rotating the product 360 degrees never leaves a silhouette edge merging into the background value.
Disabling the environment contribution visibly empties the micro-reflections, confirming it is contributing.
The background is a gradient, not a flat value, when sampled top to bottom.

creative_affordances: Panel colours can be tinted apart for a cool/warm split, and the rim can take a saturated accent colour.
The set can move from near-black to mid-grey; the fixed points are the three-panel structure and the edge separation rule.
known_limits: Every number in this profile was tuned for ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0; under a different tone-mapping curve or exposure the intensities and fog density must be re-derived, not copied.

RectAreaLight in this renderer supports neither shadows nor a physical-light distance falloff, so the contact shadow must come from another light or a baked plane; these panel intensities are authored, not photometric.
No renderer run for this record; values are authored starting points.

defaults.rationale: Product form is read from the shape of the reflections, so the three panels are specified by size in metres before intensity, and the key/fill/rim intensities of 12/4/8 give a 3:1 shaping ratio with an edge strip that reads about a stop over the key on the silhouette only. The environment stays low at 0.15 so it fills micro-reflections without washing out the panel shapes, and the background is a gradient rather than black so edges always have something to separate against at exposure 1.0. Kelvin-to-hex conversions here are authored approximations, not colorimetric transforms (2700K~#ffb46b, 3200K~#ffc58f, 4500K~#ffe4c4, 5600K~#fff4e5, 6500K~#ffffff, open shade 8000K~#cfe0ff).

key.note: main soft box; its reflection should cross the product's primary form

rim.note: narrow strip behind the product; supplies the separation edge

lights.ratio: key:fill ~ 3:1; rim reads about one stop above the key on the silhouette edge only

values.intensity_unit: three-intensity (lux-scaled for Directional/Hemisphere, candela for Point/Spot; tuned with the stated tone_mapping.exposure)

shadow.note: RectAreaLight casts no shadow here; these settings belong to the low DirectionalLight or shadow-catcher used for contact

post.dof: focus on the front face, roughly f/4 equivalent

never: a silhouette edge that merges into the background at any rotation
